_doc: Every fact Payobook Learn asserts about the product, with where it came from.
The practice company is a JavaScript fixture, not a tenant. That is what makes
it safe and it is also what makes it drift. Each entry below is a claim the
content makes; tools/check_contract.py re-reads the modules and fails when one
stops being true, naming the fixture entries and the content that quote it.
`taughtIn` is not decoration. When a check fails it is the list of things a
human has to re-read — the checker cannot know whether a renamed state key
invalidates one sentence or a whole lesson.

checks.why: The five stages ARE the lesson. If level0 is removed, renamed or re-ordered, L2's pipeline visual, the replica's board columns and every answer about 'whose gate is it at' teach a chain the product no longer has.

A PAYSLIP's chain is four stages and has no level0 — that gate belongs to the run. Drawing the run's five on a payslip stepper would send a learner looking for an Officer tier that does not exist there.

The tenant slots {{hrTierName}} and {{gmTierName}} DEFAULT to what this widget prints on the real board. A default that disagrees with the screen it names is worse than no slot at all: the tenant who never sets one reads a word in the lesson that is nowhere on their board. Pinning all five also pins the ORDER, which is what the pipeline visual draws.

L2 and m2 both teach that a rejection records who, when and WHY IN WRITING, and m2's whole reject branch rests on that written reason existing. Lose the fields and the lesson is teaching a discipline the product no longer supports.

learn.intent._capability reads these four groups directly. A rename makes every capability-gated answer fall through to its most restrictive branch — an officer would be told they cannot run a payroll, which is the confidently-wrong answer the gate exists to prevent.

Seven stations and seven screens resolve through these leaves — learn.screen reads its matchers off the leaf rather than keeping a copy. A retired leaf is a station that opens nothing and a screen the Coach can never recognise.

Pay Runs and Payslips are recognised by model as well as by action. If one leaf ever claimed the other's model the Coach would ground on the wrong screen and offer the wrong questions — confidently, which is the worst way to be wrong.

Four screens are client actions found by tag. importwizard has no sidebar leaf at all, so its tag is the ONLY way the Coach knows that screen is showing — rename it and a whole screen's content goes silently unreachable.

Full & Final, Proration and Retro are three screens served by ONE template, and their sidebar leaves resolve by these tags. The lg-* anchors mean a different set of numbers on each, so losing a tag collapses three screens' content onto whichever one still resolves.

PayAI may only offer to open something it can actually open, through this whitelist. Phase C2 re-targeted the envelope from pb_coach tours to pb_learn LESSONS, which is the change that lets this be checked at all: a tour was a registry entry in a module nobody validated against, and a lesson is a record whose key `learn.lesson` either has or has not. Both halves are pinned — the whitelist itself, and the old-tour compatibility map, whose ids are documentation of what each tour BECAME. If a lesson key here stops existing, PayAI's "Show me" opens a Journey that lands on the map and the offer was a lie.
taughtIn: every lesson key here is validated against learn_lessons.xml by pb_payroll_ai_insights/tests/test_action_envelope.py

checks.why: pw-division and pw-compute belong to pb_coach's tours AND to this registry. Either module removing one breaks the other silently, in a file neither team reads — the registry's `foreign` block records the shared claim and this is the check behind it.
taughtIn: mission m1 division and consequence steps

checks.why: pb_sidebar renders a FIXED icon set and an unknown name draws a plain circle with no error anywhere. The Journey's own leaf uses compass; lose it and the front door to the whole learning system renders as a blank dot.

The Coach's standing promise is that it never performs an action. Asserted as an ABSENCE because that is the shape of the promise: no provider, no composer, no product method in the answer path. A future port of health_learn's composer would arrive as exactly these names.

The generator refuses to write a translatable with no Vietnamese, so what is left to catch is a translation being silently REPLACED. These four are the ones where that would matter most: the standing promise, the launcher's invitation, the front door, and the name of the flagship screen.
taughtIn: every Vietnamese reader of this module

checks.why: L6 reads its rates, its base and its ceiling straight off this record, and m4 practises changing one. A renamed rate field does not break anything visibly — the cockpit simply stops showing a scheme, and the lesson keeps teaching a percentage the product no longer holds.
taughtIn: L6 steps 2-3 (who pays what, base & ceiling)

checks.why: m4's wrong option 'reuse the current policy's code' is refused BY THE DATABASE, and its recovery text says so. Lose the constraint and the mission coaches a learner away from something the product would now happily allow.
taughtIn: L6 step 6 (a rate change is a new record)
mission m4 newrecord step, option samecode

checks.why: THE fact the whole statutory lesson turns on: there is no version chain, so the policy in force is the ACTIVE one with the LATEST effective date. If the cockpit ever selected by create order or by id instead, the effective-date judgement in L6, m4 and the whichpolicy answer would all be teaching a rule the product had stopped following.
The two relief figures and the bands are what `payslip()` computes Mai's thuế TNCN from, so a rename here silently detaches the worked example from the product it claims to mirror.
taughtIn: the PIT bands on the statutory replica

checks.why: Four stations and four screens resolve through these leaves. A retired leaf is a station that opens nothing and a screen the Coach can never recognise — and it fails in the most misleading way, with the Coach saying it has no lessons for a screen that has a full one.
All four Setup leaves carry an action TAG and an empty action_xmlid, so the tag is the only thing that identifies the screen. Rename one and a whole section's content goes silently unreachable.

pb_learn adds NOTHING to studio.xml — L5 points at seven attributes that were already there, and the registry has now promoted them out of the fs-* foreign wildcard into `product`. That promotion is a claim about somebody else's template, so it is checked at authoring time as well as by the module's own registry test.

The seventeen anchors pb_learn added to the three Setup cockpits and the new-policy wizard are additive attributes in modules this one does not own. Nothing over there reads them, so a tidy-up would delete them without any test noticing — and the Coach's Show-me would then scroll to nothing.

The whichconfig answer teaches DEMO_<DIVISION>_END / _MID as a rule a prospect can rely on. It is a rule only for as long as the generator builds codes that way, and a demo user who is told a naming convention that no longer holds cannot find their own division's configuration.

The capstone's whole safety argument in one check. pb_learn may look at the product and may not touch it: the mission instructs, the learner presses Payobook's own buttons, and these predicates find out what happened by searching. A convenience that mutated — marking a run, ticking a flag, assigning a division from inside a poll loop — would turn a learning module into an actor on real payroll records, and it would arrive as exactly one of these tokens.
taughtIn: LIVE_VALUES is three keys: june_run_state, active_policy_rates, division_name — a whitelist entry with no reader is a read path nobody asked for

checks.why: mL1 hands each prospect one of these six divisions and verifies against that assignment. A renamed key silently un-assigns every existing demo user — round-robin keeps handing out a name nothing resolves — and the capstone then tells a prospect to compute a run it can never find.

Every predicate looks for a June 2026 run because June is the ONE month the demo generator leaves in draft — April and May are done and locked. Move the open month and the capstone asks a prospect to compute a period that is already closed, which the product will correctly refuse while the mission keeps waiting.
taughtIn: mission mL1 compute and submit steps

checks.why: A run's pb_division is COMPUTED from its first payslip's formula config and STORED — which is why every predicate can search on it, and why june_run_computed also counts slips: before the compute there are no slips, so there is no division, so the run the prospect is about to create cannot be found by division alone.

pb_demo pins the demo wizard to June 2026 and now also moves the user's own division to the front and preselects it. mL1's consequence card promises exactly that ('it is preselected and moved to the front of the list'), so if this seam is refactored away the mission is making a promise about a screen that no longer keeps it.
taughtIn: mission mL1 open step and consequence card

checks.why: THE fact Phase B got wrong and had to be rewritten. A vietnam.insurance.policy record does NOT price a payslip: grep the rate fields and every reader is a display, an analytic or a report. What prices the BHYT line is a PARAMETER CONSTANT on the division's formula configuration — EEHI in the demo world — referenced by the component that charges it. L6, m4, changerate and whichpolicy all now teach that separation and the reconciliation it implies; if the product ever wires the policy into computation, every one of them needs re-reading, because they would then be teaching a gap that had closed.
taughtIn: L5 step 2 (the parameters below the components)
L6 step 5 (the trace is a reconciliation, not a causation)
L6 step 7 (declaring a rate is half the job)
mission m4 consequence card, anomaly and reconcile step

checks.why: Eight more stations and eight more screens resolve through these leaves — learn.screen reads its matchers off the leaf rather than keeping a copy. A retired leaf is a station that opens nothing and a screen the Coach can never recognise, and it fails in the most misleading way: the Coach says it has no lessons for a screen that has a full one. sec_learn is NOT here on purpose — pb_learn ships that section itself.

Six of the eight new leaves carry an action TAG and an EMPTY action_xmlid, so the tag is the only thing that identifies the screen; Dashboard and Government Reports carry both. Rename one and a whole screen's content goes silently unreachable — LW and LA included, because a lesson renders over the replica but the Coach still has to know which live screen a learner is standing on.
taughtIn: screens dashboard / approvals / employees / contracts / insights / explorer / workforcean / govreports

checks.why: pb_learn adds NOTHING to pb_dashboard.xml — LW points at four attributes that were already there, and the registry has now promoted them out of the `foreign` block into `product`. That promotion is a claim about somebody else's template, and three of the four are ALSO pointed at by pb_coach's hero_path, so it is checked at authoring time as well as by the module's own registry test.

The 33 anchors pb_learn added to the seven Phase C1 cockpits are additive attributes in modules this one does not own. Nothing over there reads them, so a tidy-up would delete them without any test in those modules noticing — and the Coach's Show-me would then scroll to nothing. pb_people, pb_contracts and pb_govt_reports share the ppl-* CLASS vocabulary, which is exactly why the anchor KEYS are namespaced per screen.
taughtIn: intents wherelives / whichlane / howmanyslips / variance / rejectright / payrollready / expirysoon / whopays / whichtool / whichfilings

checks.why: LA step 6 and the rejectright answer both teach that the reject popover REQUIRES a written reason and that rejecting cancels every payslip in the run. That is a promise about this cockpit's own behaviour, not about the model's fields — the fields are pinned separately by payrun-reject-testimony — so it is checked where the learner meets it.
expect: All payslips in this run will be cancelled.

checks.why: The whichfilings answer teaches that the tiles are chosen by the ACTIVE COMPANY'S COUNTRY rather than by what Payobook can produce, and that a country with no catalogue says so instead of faking a form. Both halves live in this one provider: the country-keyed catalogue and the `available` flag behind the empty state. The five VN report keys are pinned because the fixture mirrors them by name.

The other half of the envelope: the whitelist names eight lesson keys, and this is where they are checked against the lessons this repo actually ships. A key that is whitelisted and not written is a 'Show me' button that opens the Journey map — the offer made and not kept, which is the exact failure the Coach's honesty rules exist to prevent.

The retirement, asserted as an ABSENCE because that is the shape of it. `useService("pb_coach")` THROWS when the service is missing, so a single one of those anywhere in PayAI means the module cannot be constructed on a database where pb_coach has been uninstalled — and the symptom is a chat pill that never appears, with an error in a console nobody is watching. The optional lookup (`env.services.pb_coach`) is what replaced it.

THE FACT PHASES A AND B GOT WRONG IN NINE PLACES. Rejecting does not send a run back to draft: `action_payslip_run_cancel` cascades `action_payslip_cancel` over every slip and writes the RUN to 'cancel', whose own selection label is 'Rejected' — so the board says rejected while the record says cancelled, and nothing hands the batch back to the officer. Returning it to a workable draft is `draft_payslip_run`, a DIFFERENT method gated to the Finance/GM tier. The false version taught a self-service undo that does not exist, and it taught it in the consequence cards of the two lessons about signing for money. If the product ever does wire rejection to draft, every site listed below needs re-reading, because they would then be teaching a gap that had closed.
expect: Only the Finance / GM tier can reset an approved pay run to
taughtIn: mission m2 consequence, debrief and undo step
mission mL1 consequence and submit step
the pipeline visual's branch caption in CHAINS.payrun

checks.why: LW's understanding check turns on this tile, and Phase C1 described it as 'every sign-off the company is waiting on, at every gate' — which is wrong three ways. It counts payroll.analytics rows in state 'ready', falling back to hr.payslip at level1/level2: PAYSLIPS not runs, HR and Finance only, never the Officer gate. A learner taught the false version reads 48 — one ordinary batch — as forty-eight runs, and a normal Tuesday as a crisis. The two lines are pinned together because the fallback is what actually renders on a database with no analytics rows, which is most of them.

The Insights hero has NO state filter — `_runs()` orders by date and returns whatever is newest, so a draft computed an hour ago is the headline and the state chip beside it is the only thing that says so. The department leaderboard is the opposite: it waits for a DONE run. Phase C1 taught 'analytics over the runs that are done' and 'built from the payslips themselves so it cannot disagree with a payslip' — both false, and the second one mattered most, because the board reads the STORED per-run roll-ups. If a state filter is ever added to _runs, the hero stops being able to show a draft and the whole read-the-chip lesson becomes noise.
expect: runs = Run.search(dom, order='date_end desc, id desc', limit=_RUN_SCAN)

checks.why: Phase C1 taught that no analytics screen explains WHY. The Explorer does, and it is the only one: `narrate` builds an exactly-reconciling variance waterfall between two comparable periods with an anomaly rail, and `drill` goes from any cell to the employees behind it — read from hr_payslip_line JOIN hr_payslip rather than from the fact tables, so the drill doubles as the audit trail. Teaching a capability away is worse than not teaching it: it sends somebody to export a spreadsheet for an answer the product already has.
expect: def drill(self, spec=None, series_key=None, category_key=None, page=0):

checks.why: Two different tests share one word on this screen. The KPI is with_bank over headcount; the per-ROW tick also requires a running contract. Phase C1 gave the tile the row's stricter definition, which makes it possible to read 100% payroll-ready off a band while somebody on a draft contract is about to be missing from the run — the exact failure the tile exists to warn about.
expect: 'ready_pct': round(100 * with_bank / headcount) if headcount else 0,

checks.why: 'Coming soon' means the country's own payroll module is NOT INSTALLED — `available` is the wizard model being present in the registry — not that Payobook has no filings for that country. Five countries carry catalogues. Phase C1 taught 'has not been built yet', which turns an install question for an administrator into a product limitation nobody can act on.
expect: available = bool(wizard_model) and wizard_model in self.env

checks.why: The whosees answer names who can read a wage roster, and Phase C1 included the final approver. The Employees and Contracts leaves carry officer, manager and super_admin only — a final approver signs for a total and still does not get the salary list, which is a deliberate separation and better teaching than the version that blurred it.

anchorLint.why: Content names controls by one name across the replica and the real screen. A control renamed in a template with the content still pointing at it produces a Show-me that scrolls to nothing — which is the exact 'confidently wrong' failure the registry exists to prevent.

tokenLint.why: A typo'd {{token}} renders the key itself to a learner instead of the company's pay day, and nothing anywhere says why. Unused slots are the other half: dead configuration a tenant admin can see and change to no effect.
